paragraphs.text: Drag the sidebar's global panel entries to reorder them in DeepSeek Harness.
# dsh-panel-order
Drag the sidebar's global panel entries into the order you want — the same gesture the session list
already uses. The order survives reloads.
DeepSeek Harness sorts the global panel icons in the sidebar (Plugins, Skill / MCP, Plugin Market, S
cheduled Tasks, Memory, …) by the `order` value each plugin passes when it registers into the `sideb
ar.panellist` slot. That value is fixed at registration time and there is no user-facing control for
it, while the session list right below can be reordered by dragging.
This plugin adds the missing gesture: press a panel row, drag it, drop it.
## Features

- Drag any global panel row to move it up or down.
- The drag starts only after the pointer travels

more than 4px, so a plain click still opens the panel.
- A blue line marks the insertion point while

dragging.
- Works in the expanded sidebar and in the collapsed icon rail; both use the same order.

- “More” always stays at the bottom.
- The order is saved and replayed on every page load.
- Panels
you have never dragged (for example a plugin installed later) are appended after the ones you alread

y arranged, never shuffled into the middle.
- Uninstalling restores the plain plugin-registration or
der on the next load.
## Install
### From a local checkout
Register the directory as a bundle in the profile that runs your Web UI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The CLI forwards the request to pnpm and maintains the profile's bundle list itself; do not edit the
profile manifest by hand. If you use a plugin manager UI with an “install bundle” action, point it
at the same directory.
Restart or reload the page afterwards — the bundle registers a Client module, so the browser has to
reload the page afterwards — the bundle registers a Client module, so the browser has to reload it.
### Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x with the Web UI (the desktop app, or a served web instance).
- No external
dependencies, no services, no API keys, no build step.
## Usage

1. Press and hold a row in the sidebar's global panel list.
2. Move the pointer more than 4px and ke

ep moving; the row turns translucent and a blue insertion line follows the pointer.
3. Release to dr

op. The list reorders immediately.
4. Reload whenever you like — the order is kept.
Saved order lives in `localStorage` under the key `dsh-panel-order.v1`. Clearing site data resets it

## How it works
1. Read the live panel registry through `ctx.slots.entriesOfSlot('sidebar.panellist')`, which yields

each entry's `id`, `order` and `label`.
2. On drop, write new `order` values (`0, 10, 20, …`) onto

those registration objects.
3. Bump the list slot so the sidebar recomputes its panel snapshot — reg
ister a throwaway entry and dispose it immediately — which re-renders the rows in the new order and

keeps DOM order, `Tab` order and the “More” menu consistent.
4. Persist the id sequence and replay i

`Tab` order and the “More” menu consistent.
4. Persist the id sequence and replay it on every load.
Steps 2 and 3 use internals that upstream does not document as a stable API. The failure mode if ups
tream changes them is “dragging has no effect”: the sidebar, the panels and other plugins keep worki
ng, and uninstalling the plugin leaves no trace.
## Limitations
- Rows are matched to entries by their rendered label. Two panels that expose the identical label ar

e left untouched instead of being sorted against each other.
- Panels pinned into “More” keep their

relative position; only the visible rows are reordered by a drag.
- The saved order is kept in `loca
lStorage`, which is scoped to the page origin. The desktop app serves the UI from a fixed port, so t
he order survives restarts there; a web instance started with a random port (`--port 0`) gets a new

origin and falls back to the registration order.
- No keyboard reordering yet — the drag is a pointe

falls back to the registration order.
- No keyboard reordering yet — the drag is a pointer gesture.
## Compatibility
- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x, Web UI only (the desktop app and served web instances share the Client mod

ule format).
- Upstream discussion about making panel order a first-class feature: deepseek-harness
ream discussion about making panel order a first-class feature: deepseek-harness discussions #11198.
## Development

resources, icon format and size, and the host entry point. Behavior is verified against a live Web
UI by dragging a row and reloading the page.
